newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World net below forecasts but market bullish.
newsitem.headline: New World net below forecasts but market bullish.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd's fiscal 1996 earnings were a tad below expectations but analysts said on Thursday they remained bullish on the company's outlook and saw no reason to change their views on the stock.

New World posted 1995/96 (July-June) net profit of HK$4.16 billion (US$538 million) compared to HK$3.41 billion in fiscal 1995. Analysts had expected fiscal 1996 net profit of about HK$4.2 billion to HK$4.3 billion.
Fiscal 1996 earnings included an exceptional gain of HK$1.15 billion following the spin-offs of New World Infrastructure Ltd and Renaissance Hotel Group.
"It was just slightly below expectations. But it is immaterial anyway," said Edward Chan, research director at NAVA SC Securities.

"There were a series of corporate moves at New World so I think the difference mainly comes from interest expense, tax rate and minority interest. I think, as a whole, the operating results are in line with our expectations."
Chan predicted fiscal 1997 net profit of HK$5.3 billion due to higher property sales in Hong Kong.

"In financial year 1997 we are going to see a large increase in development profits," said CS First Boston analyst Martin Tacon. He had expected fiscal 1996 net profit of HK$4.2 billion but saw no reason to lower his 1997 forecast of HK$5.4 billion.
"They have got about 65 percent of their development earnings locked in for 1997 and their development earnings make up approximately half of their total operating profit," he said.
Tacon said New World Development had already sold about 1,000 units of its Discovery Park project and other projects were being well received.
New World said it expects to have about five million square feet of development properties completed in the next two years and one million square feet of investment properties.
It said it currently has a property development portfolio of 23 projects and an investment portfolio of 12 projects.
"For the next three years, the (development project) schedule looks a lot better," said Nicholas Wong, analyst at HSBC James Capel. He expected fiscal 1997 net profit of HK$5.2 billion.
Wong said earnings growth would come from "more property development and stable growth from investment properties".
"Salisbury Garden (development) will come on stream and start to contribute and New World Infrastructure will grow by a significant percentage," Wong added.
New World Infrastructure reported net profit of HK$240.73 million for the period of January to June 1996 compared to HK$130.71 million in the same period last year.

Wong maintained a buy recommendation on New World Development and said his six-month target for the share price was HK$50 to HK$55. New World Development shares fell HK$1.10 to close at HK$46.80 on Thursday.
"There may be some technical pullback after this results annoucement," Chan said. But he maintained a buy rating and had a six-month price target of about HK$53.
"We still think the fundamental growth will attract more investor interest and there will continue to be more spin-offs of its underlying assets in the coming two years," he said.
"Basically the hidden value of this company will be a lot. In the long term we still hold our buy recommendation."
